raw_segments.text: Ignorance is a frail base for virtue.
Yet that it is the condition for which woman was organized has been insisted upon by the
writers who have most vehemently argued in favor of the superiority of man—a superiority
not in degree, but essence, though to soften the argument they have labored to prove, with
chivalrous generosity, that the sexes ought not to be compared.
Man was made to reason, woman to feel.
And that together, flesh and spirit, they make the most perfect whole, by blending happily
reason and sensibility into one character.
